name: Artemis II Orion (Integrity)
notes: Crewed lunar free-return flyby. Launch SLS 2026-04-01 22:35:12 UTC LC-39B; TLI 2026-04-02 23:49 UTC; far-side closest approach 6545 km altitude 2026-04-06 (NASA SVS 5633); CM/ESM separation 2026-04-10 23:33 UTC (ESA); splashdown off San Diego 2026-04-10 8:07 pm EDT = 2026-04-11 00:07 UTC, crew recovered (status decayed = re-entered and recovered). Horizons -1024 header (rev 2026-04-20) lists the event timeline.

name: Artemis II European Service Module (ESM-2)
notes: Separated from the crew module 11 Apr 00:33 BST (2026-04-10 23:33 UTC) and burned up in the atmosphere (ESA). Component of launch 2026-069 without its own NORAD number (GCAT deepcat D01206 'ESM-2 Bremen', D01205 Crew Module Adapter).

name: Artemis II ICPS-2 (SLS upper stage)
notes: Raised Orion to a ~185x70377 km, 23.5-h HEO (Horizons -1024 header); target of the crew proximity-operations demo; disposal burn ~2026-04-02 03:35 UTC for re-entry over the remote Pacific (NASA blog); GCAT satcat: deorbited 2026-04-02 ~23:44 UTC near 132W 24N. Regime OTHER: HEO with P<2.4 d, never translunar. No Horizons ID found.

name: TACHELES (DLR cubesat, Artemis II)
notes: Artemis II secondary payload deployed into the ~70,000 km HEO ~2026-04-02 03:39 UTC (NASA). Failed to raise perigee and re-entered at first perigee (McDowell, cited in Wikipedia Artemis II); Space-Track DECAY_DATE 2026-04-02 (GCAT 2026-04-03 00:01? UTC near 116W 23N). OTHER: HEO P~0.98 d.

name: K-RadCube (KASA cubesat, Artemis II)
notes: Korea AeroSpace Administration radiation cubesat; deployed in HEO with the other Artemis II cubesats; did not achieve perigee raise and re-entered at first perigee (McDowell 2026-04-10 via Wikipedia); Space-Track decay 2026-04-02, GCAT 2026-04-02 ~23:52 UTC near 120W 28N.

name: SWC-1 (SHAMS, Saudi Space Weather CubeSat-1)
notes: Only Artemis II cubesat that raised its perigee and stayed in orbit (McDowell via Wikipedia Artemis II); GCAT status O (in orbit) 492x70228 km; Space-Track last GP 2026-04-17, no decay. Horizons ID -168540 verified by one request: ephemeris ends 2026-04-07 14:30 UT. Operational status after April not found. OTHER: P=0.98 d.

name: ATENEA (CONAE cubesat, Artemis II)
notes: Argentine microsatellite deployed from the Orion stage adapter on Artemis II; communicated from ~70,000 km (national record) and completed its planned 20-h mission on 2026-04-02 (CONAE). Carried no propulsion (McDowell: only the other three cubesats were to raise perigee) so re-entry at first perigee ~1 d after deployment is INFERRED; not catalogued in GCAT (2026-10-17) or the cached Space-Track data.

name: SMILE
aliases: Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer;SMILE (spacecraft)
notes: ESA-CAS; Vega C VV29 2026-05-19 03:52 UTC into ~700 km LEO (Avio); reached science orbit 2026-06-20 after 12 main-engine burns, commissioning to end Aug, science from Sep 2026 (ESA/phys.org). ~5000x121000 km i~70 (Horizons header; ESA trajectory fit through 2026-08-05). Apogee >100,000 km from centre -> CISLUNAR_HEO though P=2.10 d. status_date = latest GP epoch.

name: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope
notes: Launched Falcon Heavy LC-39A 2026-08-30 11:26:04 UTC (Horizons header); ~90-day transfer, commissioning in cruise; arrays/HGA/aperture cover deployed, SE-L2 quasi-halo arrival early Dec 2026 (orbitalradar.com/roman-tracker). Horizons tracking through 2026-10-18. Geocentric osculating elements are not meaningful on the L2 transfer.

name: Falcon Heavy-013 stage 2 (Roman launch)
notes: Upper stage of the Roman launch, escaped to heliocentric orbit a=1.0205 AU e=0.0137 i=0.11 deg (ecliptic), q=1.0065 Q=1.0344 AU, Earth MOID 0.0101 AU, 313 obs 2026-08-30..10-17 (Bill Gray find_orb, elements as in neocpsat combined fit); geocentric distance 0.0166 AU on 2026-10-17; slow drift (synodic ~33 yr) -> escaped. GCAT deepcat D01207: heliocentric from ~2026-09-25. Period column left empty (heliocentric P ~376 d).

name: MMX (Martian Moons eXploration)
notes: H3 F10 (H3-24) from Tanegashima 2026-10-20 04:41:03 JST = 2026-10-19 19:41:03 UTC; separated ~71 min after liftoff onto its Earth-escape trajectory (JAXA). Mars arrival Aug 2027, Earth return 2031. Horizons -239 is JAXA's pre-launch planning trajectory V0.2 (rev 2026-10-07) - expect offsets; it gives r=8704 km at 2026-10-19 21:00 UTC and 388,136 km at 2026-10-21 00:00. Hyperbolic geocentric elements (a<0). Space-Track SATCAT 101109, no GP yet.

name: H3 F10 second stage (MMX launch)
notes: Catalogued by Space-Track with MMX (launch 2026-10-19 TNSTA, no GP sets yet). Presumed on an Earth-escape trajectory like MMX (direct injection by H3) - not confirmed by any source; no ephemeris.

name: SOHO
notes: ESA/NASA, halo orbit about SE-L1; mission repeatedly extended and continuing (NASA SOHO page); Horizons -21 revised 2026-09-01 with GSFC FDF trajectory to 2026-11-02.

name: ACE
notes: Still flying ~29 yr after launch and streaming real-time solar wind as backup to SOLAR-1 (CME Tracker observatories page, 2026); Horizons -92 revised 2026-09-30.

name: Wind
notes: Part of the existing L1 fleet with ACE (Space Sci Rev IMAP paper, 2026); Horizons -8 based on tracking through 2026-09-21 (rev 2026-09-30).

name: DSCOVR
notes: EPIC imaged three Pacific tropical cyclones 2026-09-02; operational real-time solar-wind role passed to SOLAR-1 in spring 2026 (cmetracker.ai). Horizons -78 rev 2026-10-19.

name: Aditya-L1
notes: Healthy, routine science in third year at SE-L1; station-keeping burns 2026-02-22 and 2026-06-07 (adityayaan.com); ISRO 2026-10-15 joint Aditya-L1/Proba-3 coronagraph results. Horizons -156 rev 2026-09-30.

name: IMAP
notes: Entered final SE-L1 Lissajous orbit 2026-01-10, science from 2026-02-01 (NASA SVS, eoPortal). status_date = Horizons -43 revision 2026-10-20.

name: SOLAR-1 (SWFO-L1)
notes: NOAA: renamed SOLAR-1, reached L1 (GCAT 2026-01-23) and became the operational real-time solar-wind monitor in spring 2026 (NOAA Satellites, cmetracker.ai). Horizons tracking through 2026-10-13.

name: Carruthers Geocorona Observatory
notes: 24-month primary science mission began 2026-03-01 at SE-L1 (NASA blog 2026-03-02); Horizons -171 last tracking 2026-10-19.

name: Falcon 9-518 stage 2 (IMAP launch)
notes: Launched with IMAP/SWFO-L1/Carruthers to a 217x2.27e6 km trajectory; GCAT deepcat D01196 moves it to heliocentric orbit ~Jan 2026 (date uncertain); Space-Track marks DECAY_DATE 2025-09-26 (escape bookkeeping). No ephemeris found.

name: JWST
notes: Fully operational in fifth science year, propellant for 20+ yr (orbitalradar, keeptrack 2026); Horizons -170 rev 2026-10-19.

name: Gaia
notes: Science ended 2025-01-15; left SE-L2 via burns 2025-03-07 and 2025-03-27 into a heliocentric retirement orbit avoiding Earth, passivated 2025-03-27 (ESA). Horizons scan: 7.89e7 km from Earth on 2026-09-01 (far now); EARTH_NEAR_HELIO only because it was <0.05 AU in 2025.

name: Euclid
notes: Galactic-bulge survey data release 2026-06-23, quasar discoveries 2026-07 (Euclid Consortium); Horizons -680 tracking-data based through 2026-08-31.

name: Spektr-RG
notes: Tracked at SE-L2 Jun-Oct 2026; station-keeping dV 2026-09-07 and between 2026-09-21 and 10-04 seen in find_orb fits (pluto A11GdpR/C46MLP1) -> actively controlled; primary 6.5-yr mission complete, RAS Space Council (June 2026) extended operations to 2031 (de.wikipedia citing IKI/RAS). Heliocentric ecliptic elements from the find_orb fit (as in neocpsat.tsv). Horizons has no 'Spektr-RG'/'SRG' target.

name: Chang'e-6 orbiter
notes: Extended mission after the 2024 sample return (SE-L2 in 2024, then back to cislunar space); Aug 2026 geocentric orbit q=368k Q=513k km i=74.5 P=33.7 d (pluto A11FfIf); still observed 2026-10-01 (A11Htul). No 2026 CNSA operational statement found -> unknown. Horizons: no Chang'e 6 orbiter target.

name: ESCAPADE Blue
notes: New Glenn NG-2 2025-11-13 20:45 UTC to an SE-L2 loiter orbit (Horizons header, Wikipedia). Powered Earth flyby with ~9-min trans-Mars injection burn Nov 7 2026 (Advanced Space, SmallSat 2026); Horizons predicts perigee r=8036 km (alt ~1660 km) 2026-11-07 ~10:00 UTC; ~11-month cruise to Mars. Horizons tracking through 2026-10-12. Geocentric osculating elements omitted (e~0.999, meaningless at 1.4e6 km).

name: ESCAPADE Gold
notes: Twin of ESCAPADE Blue; Earth flyby + TMI burn Nov 9 2026 (Advanced Space); Horizons perigee r=7388 km (alt ~1010 km) 2026-11-09 10:59 UTC; Wikipedia: late-2026 Earth gravity assist then Mars. Horizons tracking through 2026-10-12.

name: New Glenn NG-2 second stage (GS2)
aliases: EscaPADE STAGE;New Glenn GS2;Viasat CPS Demo (hosted)
notes: Safed after ESCAPADE deployment 2025-11-13 (Blue Origin) and nudged to slightly positive C3 (Horizons header: ballistic extrapolation of last telemetry, large errors expected); GCAT heliocentric from 2025-11-28. Horizons distance 3.0e7 km on 2027-01-05 (no near-term return).

name: LRO
notes: Operating (new-crater discovery, NASA 2026-09-16; FY2027 request funds LRO 2027-31). Horizons -85 rev 2026-10-07. Elements selenocentric (Moon body equator), period selenocentric.

name: Danuri (KPLO)
notes: Mission extended to Dec 2027 (KARI); imaged the Falcon 9 stage impact site before/after Aug 2026 (Chosun 2026-08-06). Horizons tag-up data through 2026-10-18. Elements selenocentric.

name: Chandrayaan-2 orbiter
notes: Orbiter healthy, all payloads operational (DFSAR results ISRO 2026-05-27, The Hindu 2026-05-28); Horizons data through 2026-10-18. Elements selenocentric.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Propulsion Module
notes: June 2026 geocentric orbit a=366,786 km e=0.627 i=28.6 P=25.6 d; predicted lunar passage ~28,000 km on 2026-08-19 sending it to ~1e6 km by Aug 30, near escape - probably its last apparition (pluto ZTF10FG / neocpsat). No ISRO status since 2023; Horizons -169 ends 2023-11-10.

name: CAPSTONE
aliases: Cislunar Autonomous Positioning System Technology Operations and Navigation Experiment;CAPSTONE (spacecraft)
notes: Completed NASA mission: Horizons -1176 note 2026-07-28 'no further updates', nav data through 2026-07-15, prediction to 2026-08-14. Left the NRHO/Moon end of Aug 2026 into HEO a=255,431 km e=0.285 i=36.6 P=14.87 d (pluto SK000bY, 10 obs 2026-09-12). derelict = no operations reported (actual spacecraft state unknown).

name: ARTEMIS P1 (THEMIS-B)
notes: Horizons -192 revised 2026-10-20 with trajectory to 2026-11-15 (routine navigation updates imply continuing operations); no 2026 news item found. Elements selenocentric (retrograde, i~177 deg).

name: ARTEMIS P2 (THEMIS-C)
notes: Horizons -193 revised 2026-10-20, trajectory to 2026-11-15; no 2026 news item found. Elements selenocentric.

name: Queqiao-1
notes: Still operational in its EM-L2 halo orbit relaying Chang'e-4/Yutu-2 (Selenian Boondocks 2026-04-19). No public ephemeris (Space-Track GP frozen at 2018-05-20; Horizons 'Queqiao' not found).

name: Queqiao-2
notes: Operating stably >2 yr in a 24-h elliptical frozen lunar orbit (~300x16,900 km alt, GCAT) to relay for Chang'e-7 (BeyondLEO, updated 2026-10-01); Chang'e-7 now 2027. Horizons 'Queqiao-2' not found.

name: DRO-A
notes: 2026-03-25 Zhongguancun Forum: DRO-A/DRO-B/DRO-L still experimenting after 2 yr, K-band ISL to 1.17e6 km. DRO-A in the lunar DRO (~28-d period; damaged solar arrays after launch anomaly, Aerospace Sci. Tech. 2026). Elements = Space-Track GP 2026-10-12 (SGP4 fit, geocentric, rough for a DRO).

name: DRO-B
notes: Moved from the DRO to a 3:2 Earth-Moon resonant orbit in March 2025 (Gunter's Space Page upd. 2026-09-03; Jatan Moon Monday #291: passes L3/L4/L5 regions) -> EM_OTHER; active per 2026-03-25 CAS statement. Elements = Space-Track GP 2026-09-21.

name: Tiandu-1
notes: Left lunar orbit 2025 for a geocentric HEO (GCAT); P=11.76 d q=150k Q=287k km i=34.2; post-manoeuvre batch 2026-10-01..15 -> manoeuvring/active (pluto ZTF10GU, elements as in neocpsat combined fit). Daytime lunar-distance laser ranging 2025-04-26/27 (DSEL).

name: Tiandu-2
notes: 15-kg companion of Tiandu-1, separated in lunar orbit 2024-04-03; GCAT lprcat still lists it in a ~289x10,000 km i=105 lunar orbit (status O); no 2026 report found.

name: Lunar Trailblazer
notes: Contact lost the day after the 2025-02-26 launch (solar arrays mis-pointed, batteries depleted); mission ended 2025-07-31 (NASA JPL, Horizons note). Heliocentric; Horizons distance 8.8e7 km on 2026-09-01.

name: TESS
notes: P/2 lunar-resonant orbit; operating in third extended mission (to 2028); safe mode 2026-01-15..18 recovered (TASOC DRN sector 1751). Horizons tracking through 2026-10-18.

name: IBEX
notes: NASA SVS gallery (2026-03-02) says IBEX continues to collect heliospheric-boundary ENA data; caution: Space-Track GP stale since 2025-07-25 and Bill Gray TLE ends 2026-01-01, no 2026 orbit found. Horizons 'IBEX' not found.

name: Chandra X-ray Observatory
notes: New science release 2026-10-14 (NASA); still operational (Ars Technica Oct 2026), FY2026 appropriation $63M. Apogee >100,000 km -> CISLUNAR_HEO by the numeric rule (SCHEMA lists Chandra as an HEO example; P=2.65 d).

name: INTEGRAL
notes: Science operations ended 2025-02-28; ESOC keeps monitoring it until atmospheric re-entry ~Feb 2029 (ESA, Wikipedia). Apogee ~152,000 km -> CISLUNAR_HEO by the numeric rule (SCHEMA example lists INTEGRAL under HEO).

name: MMS-1
notes: NASA FY2026 appropriation keeps >=$23M for MMS (AAS summary 2026-01-16); fresh Space-Track GP at 2026-10-21 (maneuvering formation). Apogee ~178,000 km from centre -> CISLUNAR_HEO (P=3.51 d).

name: MMS-2
notes: NASA FY2026 appropriation keeps >=$23M for MMS (AAS summary 2026-01-16); fresh Space-Track GP at 2026-10-21 (maneuvering formation). Apogee ~178,000 km from centre -> CISLUNAR_HEO (P=3.51 d).

name: MMS-3
notes: NASA FY2026 appropriation keeps >=$23M for MMS (AAS summary 2026-01-16); fresh Space-Track GP at 2026-10-21 (maneuvering formation). Apogee ~178,000 km from centre -> CISLUNAR_HEO (P=3.51 d).

name: MMS-4
notes: NASA FY2026 appropriation keeps >=$23M for MMS (AAS summary 2026-01-16); fresh Space-Track GP at 2026-10-21 (maneuvering formation). Apogee ~178,000 km from centre -> CISLUNAR_HEO (P=3.51 d).

name: Proba-3 Coronagraph (CSC)
notes: CSC anomaly 2026-02-14/15 (attitude/contact loss), fully recovered; formation flying resumed early June 2026 (Redwire, Gunter); joint Aditya-L1/Proba-3 results (ISRO 2026-10-15). OTHER: HEO 1035x60170 km alt, P=0.82 d (below 2.4 d, apogee <100,000 km). Elements from Space-Track SATCAT (no epoch). Horizons 'Proba-3' not found.

name: Proba-3 Occulter (OSC)
notes: Formation-flying partner of the CSC; formation flying resumed early June 2026 after the CSC recovery (Redwire). OTHER: P=0.82 d, apogee <100,000 km. Elements from Space-Track SATCAT (no epoch).

name: Spektr-R (RadioAstron)
notes: Communication problems from 2019-01-10, last contact 2019-01-11; recovery attempts until mid-May; mission declared finished 2019-05-30 (Wikipedia Spektr-R, Interfax Feb 2019). Still tracked: Space-Track GP 2026-10-05, Horizons -557 (TLE-based, rev 2026-10-02).

name: JUICE
notes: Second Earth gravity assist 2026-09-28 11:45:11.5 UTC at 15,018 km from Earth centre (alt ~8640 km, DLR) over the Indian Ocean, +3.5 km/s (ESA, Horizons header); next Earth flyby Jan 2029.

name: Europa Clipper
notes: Earth gravity assist 2026-12-03: Horizons -159 minimum geocentric distance 9607 km (alt ~3230 km) at 20:14 UTC (1-min scan); Wikipedia lists '4:15 PM EST' (21:15 UTC) - 1 h discrepancy, Horizons used. Jupiter arrival 2030-04-11. status_date = Horizons revision 2026-09-30.

name: Cert-2 Centaur V upper stage
aliases: Centaur V-002;VULCAN CENTAUR R/B;Cert-2 Centaur RB Booster;C43KHJ1;A11cvui;A11cvun
notes: Heliocentric since 2024-10 with inert CERT-2 payload. Bill Gray fit to 21 obs 2025-10-19..11-16 (24179a25.tle): Earth perigee 2029-02-27.42 TT q=8867+/-4574 km; 'no updates until it returns in late 2026', tle_list Warn 2026-Nov-10 -> recovery window late 2026 (no 2026 recovery reported in a web search 2026-10-21). Horizons -161448 is the old 2024 solution: min distance 8.13e6 km on 2026-12-21; daily samples put a close approach (3.4e4-1.2e5 km) on 2029-02-27, BG: 'good chance of re-entering our atmosphere on 2029 Feb 27'. Not physically close in 2026.

name: OSIRIS-APEX
notes: Extended mission to (99942) Apophis. Earth gravity assist EGA2 planned 2027-03-17 at 4146 km altitude, EGA3 2029-04-13 (1153 km, ~1 h after Apophis), arrival 2029-06-05 (PSJ 2023 mission design); Univ. Arizona (2026): team writing the command sequence for the 'next March' (2027) flyby. Horizons -64 (rev 2025-09-18) 10-min scan: min r=10,561 km (alt ~4180 km) 2027-03-16 03:30 UTC. Bill Gray tle_list Warn 2027-Feb-01 'OSIRIS-APEX flyby in March'. status_date = date of this check (operating per UA news). No Earth flyby Sep-Dec 2026.

name: P22qGC1 (unidentified Earth-flyby object)
notes: NEOCP object with Earth flyby: perigee 2026-09-22 17:08 TT, q=29,757 km in the fit (~54,000 km per note); pre-flyby heliocentric a=1.0171 AU e=0.0088 i=0.33 deg - artificial-object candidate, not identified (pluto P22qGC1; geocentric elements of the fit as in neocpsat).

name: Hayabusa2
notes: Flew by (98943) Torifune 2026-07-05 (S&T; JST: ~400 m); next Earth flybys Dec 2027 and Jun 2028, 1998 KY26 arrival 2031 (S&T, Horizons -37 header rev 2026-09-30, tracking through 2026-09-29).

name: Tianwen-2
notes: At Earth quasi-satellite 469219 Kamo'oalewa from ~July 2026, departs Apr 2027, Earth flyby with sample-capsule re-entry Nov 2027 (Scientific American, Planetary Society). Horizons 'Tianwen-2' not found.

name: Tianwen-2 CZ-3B Y110 stage 3
notes: Escaped with Tianwen-2 (launched 2025-05-28); GCAT hcocat D01190 heliocentric, no elements or ephemeris published. Included as a post-2024 Earth-departure object.

name: Falcon 9-427 stage 2 (Blue Ghost M1 launch)
notes: Long-lived lunar-perturbed cislunar orbit after the 2025-01-15 Blue Ghost M1/HAKUTO-R M2 launch; struck the Moon 2026-08-05 (~06:35 UTC, 19.6N 93.4W per GCAT/lunarmission; Horizons ephemeris ends at the surface); Danuri LUTI imaged the site before and after (Chosun 2026-08-06).
